note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Progressive left-sided hearing loss and left-sided facial numbness for ~3 weeks. No clear trigger or exposure reported.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Symptoms present for "a few weeks," approximately three weeks. Numbness described as persistent and present at time of consult.
- ENT symptoms:
  - Throat swelling/closure sensation: none reported.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: none reported.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: none reported.
  - Drooling: none reported.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: history of nasal polyps; uses an unspecified nasal spray intermittently when polyps flare.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: none reported.
  - Dyspnea: none reported.
  - Distribution of sensory change/swelling: numbness localized to left side of face around the left ear and along the left jawline; no swelling reported.
  - Ear symptoms: decreased hearing on left side; occasional tinnitus/ringing in the ear; no ear pain; no ear discharge.
  - Neck symptoms: none reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - Prior history described as "labyrinthitis" in the past (no current active labyrinthitis).
  - Known nasal polyps treated intermittently with a prescribed nasal spray (name not remembered).
  - Uses Rennies (antacid) as needed.
  - No prior hospitalizations or injection therapies documented for this problem.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: latex.
  - Current medications: nasal spray — name not documented; dose/route/frequency not documented. Rennies (antacid) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Relevant social context:
  - Occupation: jockey; symptoms (ringing and intermittent dizziness) are affecting work and training.
  - Lives with partner. Patient was in a private place and not accompanied during the video consult.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: no swelling observed or reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: no stridor, noisy breathing, or dyspnea reported.
- Mental status and associated features: patient alert and oriented; reports occasional dizziness associated with ear ringing; no syncope.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not present during the consult; patient stated she is in a private place. (Lives with partner at home but partner not present.)

Assessment:
- Clinical impression: Possible Bell's palsy suggested by clinician; requires face-to-face neurological and ENT assessment to confirm.
  - Justification: Unilateral (left) facial sensory change and ipsilateral hearing reduction with occasional tinnitus; clinician noted lack of other systemic or life-threatening features and recommended in-person neurological examination and otoscopic/ENT assessment.
- Uncertainty/conflict noted:
  - No internal conflicts identified in the transcript.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Arrange face-to-face clinic assessment today for neurological examination and ear inspection.
  - General Practitioner to assess in clinic; clinician to send message to admin team to book patient into a clinic within Central London.
  - Patient instructed to call the support team number (left in the patient's notes) five minutes after receiving the booking message to be slotted into a convenient clinic appointment.
- Specific instructions given to patient:
  - Attend the face-to-face clinic appointment today for definitive assessment and reassurance.
  - Ensure the appointment is completed today (patient acknowledged).
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - No specific emergency/red flag instructions were documented in the consult.
- Follow-up:
  - In-person ENT/neurological examination and otoscopic evaluation to be performed at the arranged clinic appointment.
  - Further management will be determined after physical examination (no additional follow-up details documented).
- COVID-19 vaccine suitability: not discussed.
- Emergency contact instructions as stated:
  - "Ring the support team number (left in the notes) after five minutes and they will slot you into a place that's convenient."
